name: Omama
role: The Yanomami creator, who made the world, the forest and the first people, and whose words the shamans still repeat.
fun_fact: In Davi Kopenawa's telling, Omama's words are still spoken by shamans, so creation is not a past event but something continually upheld.

name: Yurupary
role: Tukanoan lawgiver and ancestor whose voice sounds in the sacred flutes and trumpets, kept from women and the uninitiated.
fun_fact: The flutes are said to be made from his bones, cut from a paxiuba palm that grew out of his ashes.

name: Boa
role: The ancestral anaconda of Tukanoan tradition, whose body was the first canoe and whose journey up the rivers carried the first peoples.
fun_fact: Shipibo tellings on the Ucayali give a great boa a different role: mother of all water creatures, who once made a bridge of her body for the first people to cross.

name: Jaguar
role: In Shipibo-Konibo tradition, a person with villages and knowledge of its own, able to cross between jaguar and human form.
fun_fact: Shipibo story treats jaguars as persons with their own villages, and shamans are said to learn from them rather than only to hunt them.

name: Jaguar-Woman
role: The woman in the Shipibo tale who leaves her human skin at night and hunts as a jaguar, bringing danger to her husband and household.
fun_fact: The tale is told in more than one form: in some versions she is cured, and in others she kills her husband and returns to the forest.

name: Yaya
role: A being of the Taíno first world, whose son Yayael became fish in a calabash and whose broken gourd released the sea.
fun_fact: Pané reports that the Taíno did not know what Yaya's name meant, so the account has come down with that uncertainty intact.

name: Atabey
role: Taíno mother goddess, named by Pané as the mother of Yúcahu and invoked under several names, associated with fresh water and fertility.
fun_fact: Pané lists several names for her, among them Atabex, Yermaoguacar, Apito and Zuimaco, which may mean that several local goddesses were gathered under one figure.

name: Deminán Caracaracol
role: Taíno culture hero, first of the four brothers born from Itiba Tahuvava, who took down Yaya's gourd and carried a turtle in his shoulder.
fun_fact: His epithet Caracaracol means 'scabby', and the swelling on his shoulder is where the first turtle is said to have come from.

name: Guabancex
role: The Taíno storm power, a woman cemí who raises wind and water when angry, attended by Guataubá and Coatrisquie.
fun_fact: The Taíno word juracán, for the storm she brings, is the root of the English word hurricane.

name: Yúcahu
role: The supreme Taíno being, Yúcahu Bagua Maórocoti, who has a mother but no beginning and is linked with cassava and the sea.
fun_fact: Pané says he has a mother but no beginning, and his name is often connected with the yuca that fed the islands.
